subject: "Bouncing" range sliderInput when using controls to updateSliderInput

messages.author: f8da0a5af50e1b7e
messages.subject: "Bouncing" range sliderInput when using controls to updateSliderInput
parts:
Hi:

I'm working with a Shiny app, both developed and running in R 3.1.1 and shiny-server free version 1.1.0.10000, that has a number of range sliderInputs -- they're for setting an income range measured in % of the federal poverty level (just FYI) in a tabbed interface, so each tab gets its own uniquely-named FPL slider. eg, for the insurance ("ins") tab:

sliderInput("ins_income_group1",
   label="Use the Sliders to Select an Income Range (FPL%)",
   min= 0, max = 5,step=0.05, value=c(0,5), format="0%", ticks=FALSE)

These sliders have worked reliably, without the goofy behavior that inspired my question.

I added a pair of checkboxes to set a lower or upper bound, partly because it's not easy to land perfectly on 138% and partly because our step value of 5% is handy for other reasons:

#in ui.R
checkboxInput("ins_fpl138floor", "Set lower end of FPL range to 138%", FALSE),
checkboxInput("ins_fpl138ceil", "Set upper end of FPL range to 138%", FALSE)

# to keep server.R tidy, each tab's code is called via source(), eg source("tab_insurance.R", local=TRUE)
# here's how observe & updateSliderInput are coded in tab_insurance.R:
      observe({
        val_floor <- ifelse(input$ins_fpl138floor,1.38,input$ins_income_group1[1])
        val_ceil <- ifelse(input$ins_fpl138ceil,1.38,input$ins_income_group1[2])
        updateSliderInput(session, "ins_income_group1", value=c(val_floor,val_ceil))
      })

The checkboxes function as expected -- they set the upper (lower) value to 138% when ticked, "pull" back to 138% when ticked if the user selects a different value, and leaves the slider along when unticked. However, if you click and drag on one of the slider values, the slider will bounce between that value and some other value -- the "other" value isn't anything we've hardcoded or would otherwise expect to see -- a little faster than once per second. The other value on the range slider stays put.

We've reproduced this behavior on two different machines, in recent versions of Firefox and Chrome, and confirmed that we don't get this behavior when we remove the updateSliderInput code -- that is, the checkboxes alone aren't the issue. We've not had time, yet, to run locally, dig into logs, or do other sensible things -- we will, as time permits -- but perhaps the description of the symptoms and something about my code will reveal the answer to a more experienced/savvy Shiny programmer.

Cheers!
Colin Odden
Ohio State University
